claims.text: Controlled annealing can induce nanoscale modulation of chemical disorder in rare-earth-free high-entropy alloys.
Nanoscale modulation of chemical disorder can enhance magnetostructural coupling.
Enhanced magnetostructural coupling promotes a sharp magnetic phase transition at low applied fields.
A sharp low-field magnetic transition produces a strong magnetocaloric response.
The proposed modification can preserve rapid heat transfer, low hysteresis, and mechanical stability.
The as-cast baseline has a homogeneous microstructure and moderate magnetocaloric properties.
Sub-critical annealing is intended to introduce nanoscale chemical heterogeneity and local strain fields without coarsening the microstructure.
Nanoscale chemical heterogeneity and associated local strain fields enhance magnetoelastic coupling.
Annealing-induced fluctuations in local composition and strain amplify magnetoelastic coupling.
Amplified magnetoelastic coupling sharpens the magnetic phase transition at low applied fields.
The sharpened transition produces a larger magnetic entropy change.
Retained metallic continuity maintains rapid thermal conduction after annealing.
Retained microstructural integrity maintains low magnetic hysteresis and mechanical robustness after annealing.
Relative to the as-cast baseline, annealed samples will initiate a strong magnetocaloric effect at lower applied fields.
Annealed samples will maintain or improve heat-exchange rates relative to the as-cast baseline.
Annealed samples will exhibit minimal magnetic hysteresis and robust mechanical performance.
The as-cast homogeneous baseline requires higher magnetic fields to obtain its moderate magnetocaloric response.
The proposed mechanism should extend to high-entropy alloys having comparable configurational entropy and similar magnetic-mechanical alloying strategies.
The mechanism may cease to apply when major compositional or processing changes make phase separation or grain-boundary creep dominant.
